function.name: describe_position
function.description:
What is on the board now, in words: where each side's pieces stand, material,
castling, check and the last move. For "what's the position?", "what's on the
board?", "where are my pieces?". Who is winning is `evaluate_position`.

function.name: evaluate_position
function.description:
Stockfish's verdict on who is better, from the player's side: centipawns
(positive means the player is ahead) or a forced mate and who delivers it,
with the line the engine expects. For "who's winning?", "how am I doing?",
"is this good for me?". What is on the board is `describe_position`.

function.name: get_best_moves
function.description:
Stockfish's top n moves, best first, each scored from the player's side
with the line it leads to. For a hint or advice: "what should I play?", "any
ideas?", "give me a hint".

n.description: How many candidate moves to return.
n.title: N

function.name: analyze_last_move
function.description:
Judge one move against Stockfish's best from the same position: centipawn
loss, a verdict (good/inaccuracy/mistake/blunder), the best move, and what
each took. For "how good was that move?", "was that a mistake?", "what should
I have played?". Defaults to the player's own last move; pass a color for
that side's last move.

function.name: review_game
function.description:
Review the whole game so far: each side's accuracy, how many good moves,
inaccuracies, mistakes and blunders each played, and each side's worst moves
with the better alternative. For "how did I play?", "review the game", "where
did I go wrong?".

function.name: make_move
function.description:
Play the player's move: the `legal_moves` entry their words name, as SAN
('Nf3') or UCI ('g1f3'). Map loose phrasing to the matching entry ("push the
queen's bishop pawn one square" → 'c3') and fix voice slips ("e 4" → 'e4').
For "e4", "knight to f3", "take the pawn", "castle". A move that cannot be
played is refused, and nothing moves.

The engine answers as soon as your move lands, without being asked.
If you proposed a move and the player accepts ("yes"), call it now;
announcing a move in words is not making it.

source.description: said_the_move: the player's words say the piece or square. picked_by_position: they chose by position or number in a list ('the first one', 'the second option').

function.name: undo
function.description:
Take back the player's last move. For any normal takeback ("undo",
"take that back", "undo the bishop move") omit the arguments — the app
pops the whole exchange itself, leaving the player to move again. When
the player names several moves to take back, call this again for each
further named move. When they point back to a move by its number, pass
before_move.

before_move.description: The move number of one of the player's moves, as review_game numbers them: go back to just before it, however far back that is.
before_move.title: Before Move

function.name: new_game
function.description:
Start a new game from the starting position. For "new game", "start over",
"let's play again". Pass `player_color` when they pick a side ("I'll play
black"). Call it right away: when a game is in progress the app asks the
player to confirm.

function.name: resign
function.description:
Resign the game for the player, or for `color` when they name a side. For "I
resign", "I give up", "you win". Call it right away: when a game is in
progress the app asks the player to confirm.

function.name: claim_draw
function.description:
Claim a draw the rules allow: threefold repetition or the fifty-move rule.
For "claim a draw", "that's threefold". Call it right away: the app asks the
player to confirm. A draw by agreement is `offer_draw`.

function.name: offer_draw
function.description:
Offer the engine a draw by agreement. The engine decides; the result says
whether it accepted and, if not, why. For "draw?", "call it a draw?", "split
the point?". Once per turn, and never answer for the engine. A draw the rules
allow claiming is `claim_draw`.

function.name: export_pgn
function.description:
Export the game as PGN. For "export the game", "give me the PGN". The app
shows the player the notation with a copy button, so the reply only says it
is ready.

function.name: save_game
function.description:
Save the game under a name (default 'autosave'). For "save the game", "save
this as opening". The saves that exist are in the state; replacing one asks
the player first.

function.name: resume_game
function.description:
Load a saved game by name (default 'autosave'). For "load my game", "resume
opening". Call it right away: when a game is in progress the app asks the
player to confirm.

function.name: set_difficulty
function.description: Set how hard the engine plays: pass exactly one of tier (named level: beginner ~500, casual ~1000, intermediate ~1500, advanced ~2000, maximum = full strength), skill_level (0-20), elo (1320-3190), or step (one named level up or down from the current one). Prefer tier unless the player names a number or asks for a step. This is the only thing that changes how hard the engine plays — there is no softer or sharper style to switch to. The setting persists and the player owns it: if they ask for an easier game but rule out changing the difficulty, there is nothing left to change — say so and ask, do not call this.

function.name: set_verbosity
function.description:
Set how much the app says back: low is one short line, normal is the default,
high adds a remark on the position. The player owns this setting and it
persists: any ask to talk more or less — "talk less", "be briefer", "chattier
please" — is this call, not a change of style in one reply.

function.name: set_voice_output
function.description:
Turn spoken (TTS) output on or off. For "read your replies out loud", "turn
the voice off".

function.name: lookup
function.description:
Look something up in the chess notes: openings and their ideas, strategy,
tactics, endgames, the rules, and chess history. For "what's the idea behind
the Sicilian?", "why is the bishop pair good?", "how does en passant work?",
"who was Capablanca?". This game's position, who is winning and the best move
are the other tools.

query.description: What to look up, in a few words, naming the opening or topic.
query.title: Query

function.name: ask_player
function.description:
Ask the player to choose, when their words fit more than one
legal move. Nothing moves; the question goes to the player. Give
only the parts they said and the app asks with exactly the moves
that fit: "move my king's knight" is piece and which; "push the e
pawn" is piece and which; "take the pawn" is takes, with no piece;
"castle" is castle.

which.description: Which one, only if the player said: its square ('e2'), its file ('e'), the side it started on ('kings', 'queens'), or its square colour ('light', 'dark').

to.description: The square it goes to, only if the player said one.

takes.description: The piece it captures, only if the player said to take one.

castle.description: True when the player asked to castle.

function.name: get_board_state
function.description:
Current position: FEN, side to move, whether the game is over,
and the outcome if it is.

function.name: get_legal_moves
function.description: All legal moves in the current position, in SAN.

function.name: get_move_history
function.description: Moves played so far, in SAN, in order.

function.name: get_captured_pieces
function.description: Piece symbols each color has captured so far, in capture order.
